'''Germano D'Abramo''' (born 25 May 1973) is an Italian [[mathematician]], [[physicist]] and discoverer of [[minor planet]]s.<ref name="springer-Dabramo" />
 
== Career ==

In the late 1990s, he has been a collaborator of the [[Spaceguard Foundation]] which observes and studies [[near-Earth objects]] (NEOs), modelling NEO-populations and maintaining the foundation's online observation platform, the ''Spaceguard Central Node''.<ref name="springer-Dabramo" /> He is credited by the [[Minor Planet Center]] with the co-discovery of three minor planets he made in collaboration with astronomer [[Andrea Boattini]] at [[Pistoia Mountains Astronomical Observatory]] in April 1999.<ref name="MPC-Discoverers" />

At the beginning of 2006, he discovered a classical [[Recursion|recursive]] probabilistic solution of [[Turing]]'s [[halting problem]], published in ''Chaos, Solitons & Fractals''.<ref name="Turing" /> Since 2008, he is also involved in theoretical research on the status of and the challenge to the [[second law of thermodynamics]]. He works at the IASF research facility (''Istituto di Astrofisica Spaziale e Fisica Cosmica'') of the [[National Institute for Astrophysics]] in Rome.{{citation needed|date=June 2016}}

== Awards and honors ==

The outer main-belt asteroid [[16154 Dabramo]] is named in his honour.<ref name="springer-Dabramo" /><ref name="jpldata-Dabramo" />
